cards.explanation: The answer is False. David prays, “save me by Your righteousness.” (Psalm 31:1) That's the LORD's righteousness, not David's. A king could point at himself when he needs rescue, and David points at God instead. I think that's a habit worth stealing.

The word is fortress. David says, “For You are my rock and my fortress…” (Psalm 31:3) A rock and a fortress, two solid things stacked together. When David wants to say safe, he doesn't reach for anything soft.

The answer is the LORD's name. David says, “lead me and guide me for the sake of Your name.” (Psalm 31:3) He asks the LORD to be his guide, and he ties it to God's name. Hand the map to the One who knows the road, friends.

The answer is the LORD. David says, “You free me from the net laid out for me, for You are my refuge.” (Psalm 31:4) Somebody set a trap, and David names the One who gets him out of it. That's the third time refuge shows up in four verses, so David is really leaning on that word.

The answer is that the LORD has redeemed him. David says, “Into Your hands I commit my spirit; You have redeemed me, O LORD, God of truth.” (Psalm 31:5) He hands over his spirit and names what the LORD has done in the same breath. Jesus prays that first line from the cross (Luke 23:46).

The answer is True. David says, “I hate those who cling to worthless idols, but in the LORD I trust.” (Psalm 31:6) Watch that little word “but.” On one side are people holding tight to worthless idols. On the other side, David puts his trust in the LORD.

The word is affliction. David says, “…You have seen my affliction; You have known the anguish of my soul.” (Psalm 31:7) The LORD saw the hard part, and that's what David is glad about. Being seen in the hard part is no small thing, friends.

The answer is that his sorrow makes his eyes fail. David says, “my eyes fail from sorrow, my soul and body as well.” (Psalm 31:9) The sorrow reaches his eyes, then his soul and body too. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the psalm, and David doesn't hide it.

The word is bones. David says, “my iniquity has drained my strength, and my bones are wasting away.” (Psalm 31:10) He names his own iniquity out loud and doesn't dress it up. I think this verse hurts.
The answer is False. David says, “…they flee when they see me on the street.” (Psalm 31:11) Instead of hurrying over to help, his friends head for the exit. I think this one stings.

The answer is a broken vessel. David says, “I am forgotten like a dead man, out of mind. I am like a broken vessel.” (Psalm 31:12) Two hard pictures, back to back. I think he's saying he feels pretty useless.

The answer is True. David says, “They conspire against me and plot to take my life.” (Psalm 31:13) It's the same verse with the slander and the terror on every side. So this is more than gossip. I think David's life is on the line.

The answer is that he trusts in the LORD. David says, “But I trust in You, O LORD…” (Psalm 31:14) Slander, terror, plots, and then comes that little word “But.” That “But” is doing some heavy lifting, friends.

The answer is his times. David says, “My times are in Your hands…” (Psalm 31:15) Back in verse 5 it was his spirit, and here it's his times. Hands again, friends. His spirit and his times both rest with the LORD.
The answer is False. David says, “Make Your face shine on Your servant…” (Psalm 31:16) Shine, not hide. David is asking for the light.

The answer is that the lying lips be silenced. David says, “May lying lips be silenced…” (Psalm 31:18) These are lips that speak with arrogance against the righteous, full of pride and contempt. I think this one hurts.

The word is fear. David says, “How great is Your goodness which You have laid up for those who fear You…” (Psalm 31:19) Goodness laid up, like something saved and set aside. That's a storeroom worth knowing about, friends.

The answer is in the secret place of His presence. David says, “You hide them in the secret place of Your presence from the schemes of men.” (Psalm 31:20) The hiding spot is God's own presence. Best hiding spot I've ever heard of, friends.

The answer is False. David says, “Blessed be the LORD, for He has shown me His loving devotion in a city under siege.” (Psalm 31:21) A city under siege, not a quiet one. He blesses the LORD for loving devotion right in the middle of it.

The answer is True. David says he said in alarm, “I am cut off from Your sight!” Then, “But You heard my plea for mercy when I called to You for help.” (Psalm 31:22) He said it in alarm, and the LORD heard him anyway. Alarm can do a lot of talking, friends.
The word is faithful. David says, “The LORD preserves the faithful, but fully repays the arrogant.” (Psalm 31:23) Two groups, two different ends. He says it to all the LORD's saints.

The answer is strong and courageous. The last line says, “Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.” (Psalm 31:24) After all those heavy verses, David ends by lifting people up. That's a good place to land, friends.
